author: Daniel Sparks
headline: The S&P 500 Fell in Both September and October for Only the 17th Time Since 1950. Here's What Usually Followed.
summary: The S&P 500 experienced back-to-back monthly losses in September and October 2026 (down ~0.5% and ~0.9% respectively), marking only the 17th occurrence since 1950. Historical analysis shows that in 12 of 16 past cases, the index gained in November-December with a median gain of 3.7%, and was higher 12 months later in 14 of 16 cases. However, the author notes that this pattern is similar to normal years and the current high valuation (CAPE ratio of ~41) warrants modest expectations for buy-and-hold investors.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The article recommends buy-and-hold investors continue regular contributions to index funds like this ETF despite recent declines, suggesting it remains a sound long-term investment strategy regardless of short-term market volatility.

summary: An investment comparison between SpaceX and Micron Technology for a 5-year holding period. SpaceX, despite impressive operational achievements like reusable rockets and Starlink's growth, faces stock volatility (swinging nearly 50% from peak) and concentration risk with Elon Musk controlling 82% of voting power while owning less than half the economic stake. Micron is favored due to record fiscal 2026 revenue of $133.19 billion, $100 billion in contracted minimum revenue locked in through 16 strategic customer agreements with cash deposits, and a quarterly dividend. The author concludes Micron is the easier buy-and-hold pick despite both companies riding durable trends.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While SpaceX has genuine operational achievements (reusable rockets, Starlink with 13.6M subscribers), the stock is rated negatively for investment purposes due to extreme volatility (dropped ~40% from peak of $226 to $105 within months), concentrated control risk with Musk holding 82% voting power while owning less than half economic stake, and uncertainty tied to Musk's divided attention across multiple ventures (Tesla, X, xAI).

Micron is rated positively based on record fiscal 2026 revenue of $133.19 billion, $100 billion in contracted minimum revenue locked in through 16 multiyear take-or-pay agreements with customers, $22 billion in customer cash deposits securing supply commitments, strong AI data center memory demand, quarterly dividend payments, and predictable revenue visibility extending years into the future.

Tesla is mentioned only as one of multiple ventures managed by Elon Musk alongside SpaceX, used to illustrate the concentration risk and divided attention concern for SpaceX investors. No direct investment recommendation or analysis of Tesla is provided.
